note: Records published to the map. A record reaches the public surface by appearing here and nowhere else. Each row names the district file it is read from, and may state the sector it belongs to when the scraper's keyword rule got it wrong — the data's own caveat says category is derived from notice wording and 'needs editorial confirmation', so an override is the confirmation, recorded with its reason. Nothing here invents a record: every id exists in that district's signals.json with its own source link.
selection: One record per sector, best first, across the three pilot districts. Infrastructure is deliberately a single pin: Amravati publishes twenty-five near-identical land-acquisition notices and Nagpur two hundred and seventy, and putting them all on the map said 'something is happening in Vidarbha' and nothing else. The other sectors are what the three districts actually have — a ring road, a national highway and a railway line, a sewage plant and a tanker tender, a Housing-for-All plot list, three irrigation schemes and a river barrage, a new Collector’s office, and a sand-group clearance. Nagpur is the third district and earns three pins rather than a proportional share of three hundred: what it adds is a mode and two schemes the other two do not have — rail, a barrage, and the Gosikhurd command area that its archive is mostly about.

records.note: The single infrastructure pin. Village-precision, plain-Marathi card, notice window open into 2027 — the best-evidenced of the twenty-five.
Pune Ring Road, Alandi. An award, so the acquisition is being executed rather than proposed.
NH-548-D at Shikrapur. A second transport record because it is a different project at a different stage, not a repeat of the first.

records.why: The notice acquires land 'for STP and 12m road'. The keyword rule saw the road and filed it under transportation; the sewage treatment plant is what is being built.
Drinking-water supply by tanker to scarcity-affected villages. The rule matched 'water supply' inside the infrastructure pattern; the subject is water, not construction.
Housing for All 2022 at Mauja Sawaipura. The rule matched 'housing' inside the infrastructure pattern, which is where every Amravati housing notice ended up.

records.note: Nira Devghar irrigation project at Parhar Khurd, Bhor — the scheme is named by the notice itself.
A new Additional District Collector office at Achalpur — a public system being created, stated plainly by the notice.

records.why: Environmental consultants appointed for clearance of the district's sand groups. The rule fell through to the public-systems default; the notice is about environmental clearance of minor minerals.

records.note: The Wardha–Nagpur third and fourth railway lines at Wathoda. The first rail record on the map — every other transportation pin is a road — and the notice names the line outright.

records.why: The notice acquires land ‘for Kanhan River Project (Kochhi Barrage)’. The keyword rule read ‘agricultural land’ and the barrage together and filed it under agriculture; the land is agricultural but what is being built is a barrage on the river Nagpur draws its water from.

records.note: Gosikhurd irrigation project at Ruyad, Kuhi — a section 19 declaration, so the land is confirmed as required. Kuhi and Bhiwapur hold 166 of the archive’s 305 rows between them, and Gosikhurd is why; this is the pin that says so.
